fullIR1OptInBoundary.question: Preserve current N14 three grading IDs for a three-slot row using three serial IR1 nodes under the same stage/derivation.
schemaFacts: IR1 node schema has one optional interaction, not an interaction array. Each interaction targets its own one or multiple equivalent insertion slots. slotIds does not create multiple independently graded interactions.

Represent independent three grading IDs as three nodes retaining each interaction ID/expected key. Prior resolved node result is an explicit requires dependency. For each successive node, prior correct entries may be displayed as known math, current entry is the only answerSlot, future entries must remain static math square with no interactive ID.
This changes current simultaneous three-button row into cumulative serial local judgments. It is not an exact preservation of the old physical row/input affordance.
rendererFacts: GuidedMathReadingFlow frontier is first unresolved node; current stage nodes up to frontier are rendered cumulatively, not merged by same derivationId. No built-in general dedup of these three versions exists without transformationData grouping.
blank can address any item ID in its block; putting future interactive IDs in an earlier node would make those future buttons operable. Do not model future unknowns as real answerSlots.

renderNode removes resolved before rows only when block id starts n.id+interaction naming convention (literal prefix n.id+"-interaction"); other before rows remain alongside after. Design before/after IDs to prevent unintended duplicate equation displays.

History past stages renders all nodes as solved, and collapsed result uses the last stage node after. Last result must include the complete three-sided equation and connecting explanation; intermediate partial rows must not be mistaken for final results.
numberingAndIdentity: W036 materialize.mjs explicitly reassigns equationNumbers by node, which would multiply logical-row numbering when splitting one original row into three nodes. Use an explicitly reviewed stable logical-row map/group to preserve intended numbers; same stage/derivation name alone does not achieve this.

Preserve existing item IDs and correct keys; give distinct semantic/token and generated state block IDs. Old block ID retained/aliased exactly once where required, not copied across repeated rows. Generic ID/order/patch guards may reject the structural change and must not be silently bypassed.
